A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LatSearch work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Content can be matched reliably across pagination and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original VBench-2.0 experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, reward-prediction evaluations, and a human preference study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds CogVideoX evaluations, video-length and resolution experiments, and reward-approximation-error analysis.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same reward-model architecture, similarity-weighted supervision, regression/preference losses, unique resampling, and cumulative final pruning. The additional backbone experiments do not document an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: VBench-2.0 and the text-to-video task are retained, but new Table 6 extends generation scenarios to 3–5-second videos and 720p output beyond v1's stated short, 480p setting. No new prompt dataset or application domain is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds unmodified CogVideoX-2B and CogVideoX-5B as evaluated baselines against their respective LatSearch variants. The main competing search and noise-optimisation methods—FreeInit, FreqPrior, VideoReward, and EvoSearch—remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The evaluation settings expand to CogVideoX-2B/5B, longer outputs, and 1280×720 resolution. Appendix C.1 adds a test-set protocol measuring MSE between recovered final-reward estimates and actual final rewards across denoising steps. Existing training and benchmark protocols remain stated as before. Table 6's 32-frame default conflicts with Section 4.1's retained 33-frame specification, so an actual change to the original default experiment is unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens diagnostic validation through length/resolution scalability tests and a new analysis of cosine-based credit assignment. Figure C.1 examines final-reward recovery error across denoising steps on Wan2.1-1.3B and CogVideoX-2B. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, training curves, and human evaluation are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the seed-42 statement and existing runtime uncertainty reporting. The added results introduce no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 3 comparisons report baseline/LatSearch averages of 45.13/48.14 for CogVideoX-2B and 48.13/50.21 for CogVideoX-5B. Table 6 adds longer-video and 720p results, while Figure C.1 adds decreasing reward-recovery MSE curves. Table 4 corrects three baseline component scores and its average from 52.58 to 51.90; the runtime table's baseline score changes from 51.82 to 51.90. These are new-setting results and numerical corrections; the headline Table 1 results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, objectives, and search rules are unchanged. The new approximation-error analysis is empirical, without new assumptions, derivations, proofs, or guarantees. Section 6 retains the lack of formal convergence or optimality guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same latent-reward/RGRP contributions and comparable-or-better quality with up to 79% runtime reduction. The additional experiments support the existing claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the CogVideoX results as evidence of cross-family applicability while acknowledging variation across dimensions. It newly notes smaller gains for longer and higher-resolution generation and interprets declining reward-recovery error as support for the cosine-based proxy. The formal limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: The acknowledgments newly identify Queen Mary's Apocrita HPC facility. Existing A100 hardware information, training hyperparameters, baseline implementation details, and project access information are retained. Detailed implementation or reward-model transfer settings for the new CogVideoX experiments are not supplied.

R1.justification: The same 64 references and related-work positioning are retained. CogVideoX was already cited in v1; its new evaluation does not introduce a new citation or substantive novelty argument.

P1.justification: The Adaptability discussion is locally rewritten as Generalisation Across Backbones, with additional scalability and approximation-error paragraphs and acknowledgments. The main narrative, section order, and appendix organisation remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 is expanded, a length/resolution Table 6 and approximation-error Figure C.1 are added, and some table emphasis and headers change. The original runtime table becomes Table 7, and the existing training curves become Figure C.2. Qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The added cross-family and harder-generation evaluations strengthen empirical support for applicability, and the new reward-error diagnostic examines an important modelling approximation. Corrected baseline scores improve internal consistency. These benefits are limited by sparse implementation details for the added experiments and the new 32-versus-33-frame reporting discrepancy; the core method and headline evidence remain unchanged.
